function: Joint AAV transmit beamforming, passive RIS phase shifts and common-private rate-splitting ratio, learned to maximise secrecy energy efficiency in a cognitive satellite-aerial-terrestrial network (p. 7).
system: GEO satellite and AAV with 4-antenna ULA serving 3 single-antenna users; passive reflecting RIS of 10 elements, b-bit phases; 28 GHz (pp. 3-4, 12).
method: Reinforcement learning: PPO actor-critic with LSTM feature extractor and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck exploration noise (LSTM-PPO), trained from environment interaction; no pretraining or fine-tuning (pp. 9-10).
data_channel: No dataset; custom simulator: 3D Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channels (AAV-user, RIS-user, AAV-RIS), satellite link with rain attenuation; agent trained and evaluated in it (p. 4).
test_conditions: Training and evaluation in one simulated setting (Table II); curves versus AAV power, RIS elements and users; no stated test on unseen scenarios (pp. 12-13).
baselines: Learned: PPO with CNN, DDQN, DDPG, SAC (p. 11); own variants FAB (fixed MRT beamforming), FPB (fixed RIS), RPB (random RIS) (p. 12); no classical optimisation algorithm.
metrics: Secrecy energy efficiency (SEE), average worst-case achievable secrecy rate, average reward, and running time in seconds (pp. 11-13).
complexity: Training complexity O(N^epi Tmax(ZI ZL + ZL^2 + sum Zf Zf+1)) (p. 10); running time 780-1027 s for T=60-100 (Table III, p. 12).
q1_support: p. 4: "3D Salen-Valenzula (SV) channel [47]" - a custom Saleh-Valenzuela simulator (satellite fading classes on p. 11 follow [66]); no 3GPP TR 38.901 or 38.811, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "with parameters set as K = 10," - each sweep is a separate fixed configuration; p. 10 leaves changed numbers of VUs or RIS elements to future work; no model trained on one setting is tested on another.
q3_support: p. 11: "we compare its training results with other well-known DRL strategies" - the learned baselines (PPO-CNN, DDQN, DDPG, SAC) are compared only on training convergence (Fig. 4) and running time (Table III); SEE and rate curves (Figs. 6-9) compare only own variants FAB, FPB, RPB.
q4_support: p. 11: "the running time of the programme shown in Table III" (LSTM-PPO 780.41 to 1026.93 s, Table III on p. 12); p. 10: "Complexity and Convergence Analysis" gives O(ZI ZL + ZL^2) per LSTM step and a total training order O(N^epi Tmax(...)).
q5_support: p. 10: "We obtain the numerical results through extensive simulations" - own simulator and parameters (Table II, p. 12); no code or data link, no availability statement, no public channel dataset or measured data.
notes: Area 6 rather than 3: learned AAV beamforming, RIS phases and power splitting on an aerial link of a satellite-aerial-terrestrial network (tie-break order 6 before 3). AAV is fixed (p. 3, footnote 1), so no trajectory learning. q3 for the reviewer: the average reward of Fig. 4 is SEE-based but is a training curve. Figure numbers in the text of Sec. V are shifted by one relative to the figures.
